notes: Setup: the sandbox Node was v22.23.5 and bootstrap requires Node 24+; used the preinstalled /opt/node24 (v24.22.3). The first bootstrap attempt with Node 22 failed immediately. Bootstrap npm,submodule,reference with --allow-unpinned-reference took 177s (npm 8.6s, submodule 7.1s, reference build the rest). Baseline typecheck+lint+boundaries+video-operator-registry test: 59s, green (8 tests).
The differential file runs in about 19s with --maxWorkers=1 on 4 vCPUs; the unit file in under 1s.

Every pixel-comparing differential test is gated to linux-x64 with it.skipIf under a constant title: the kernel is single-precision float and macOS arm64 contracts multiply-adds. The defaults are not an identity natively (measured on the full 256^3 cube), so the default case is float-sensitive too. No macOS difference was measured here; the gate is a precaution.
Mutations dropping Math.fround (double throughout) or reordering the luma sum fail both the kernel and the cube tests.

Native defect: with non-writable input (split outputs) and more than one slice job, vibrance_slice8 offsets gbrp source rows by the output linesize and vibrance_slice8p's alpha store for rgb24/bgr24 (aoffset 3) races with the next slice when the output linesize equals 3*width; native output then changes with thread count and between runs. Not mirrored; tests compare those graphs against -filter_complex_threads 1. Note -filter_threads does not govern -filter_complex graphs; -filter_complex_threads does.

Native negotiates every one of the 17 negotiation sources to a format with storage (gray/YUV -> rgb24, yuva420p -> argb), so registry examples need no format= prefix; three use one anyway to cover gbrp, rgba and bgr24.
